nodes.name: Thermal injection sulfidation
nodes.procedure: The Ni NPs (0.3 g) and TEG solvent (20 mL) were introduced into a three-necked flask. When the temperature reached 180°C, 2 mL of 2-mercaptoethanol was injected into it, and then the temperature was maintained for 20 min. After the reaction, the product was washed with ethanol and dried at 60°C under vacuum to gain the Ni@Ni3S2 NPs.
nodes.source_text: 4.2. Synthesis of Ni@Ni3S2 NPs. The Ni NPs (0.3 g) and TEG solvent (20 mL) were introduced... dried at 60°C under vacuum to gain the Ni@Ni3S2 NPs.

nodes.name: NM cleaning
nodes.procedure: NM was ultrasonically cleaned in pure water, dilute hydrochloric acid (36% concentrated hydrochloric acid and pure water were mixed evenly in a volume ratio of 1:3), acetone, and alcohol, and then dried at 60°C under vacuum for 8 h to obtain clean NM.

nodes.name: Ni3S2/NM-I synthesis
nodes.procedure: The synthesis method of Ni3S2/NM-I was the same as that of Ni@Ni3S2 NPs [The Ni NPs (0.3 g) and TEG solvent (20 mL) were introduced into a three-necked flask. When the temperature reached 180°C, 2 mL of 2-mercaptoethanol was injected into it, and then the temperature was maintained for 20 min. After the reaction, the product was washed with ethanol and dried at 60°C under vacuum.], requiring only the replacement of Ni NPs with a piece of clean NM (1 cm × 3 cm). The Ni3S2/NM I catalyst used in the AWE exhibited a size of 2 cm × 2 cm or larger. The synthesis method was consistent, requiring only proportional amplification of the amount of TEG and 2-mercaptoethanol.
nodes.source_text: 4.3. Synthesis of Ni3S2/NM I. The synthesis method of Ni3S2/NM-I was the same as that of Ni@Ni3S2 NPs...

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)2/NM
nodes.procedure: 2.25 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol of urea, 4 mmol of NH4F, and 35 mL of pure water were mixed to form a uniform solution and poured into an autoclave with a volume of 45 mL. Two pieces of NM (1 cm × 3 cm) were also added to it and maintained at 120°C for 6 h to synthesize the Ni(OH)2/NM precursor.
nodes.source_text: 4.4. Synthesis of Ni3S2/NM-H. 2.25 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol of urea... maintained at 120°C for 6 h to synthesize the Ni(OH)2/NM precursor.

nodes.name: Ni3S2/NM-H sulfidation
nodes.procedure: Then, a piece of Ni(OH)2/NM was added into a 45 mL autoclave containing a solution of 25 mL of alcohol and 2.5 mL of 2-mercaptoethanol, followed by heating at 150°C for 5 h. Finally, the Ni3S2/NM-H sample was obtained after cleaning with pure water and drying under vacuum.

nodes.description: 100 h chronopotentiometry HER/OER at 100 mA cm⁻² in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: During a 100 h chronopotentiometry test of catalyst-coated carbon paper (CP) electrodes at 100 mA cm⁻² in 1.0 M KOH, both HER and OER performances exhibit initial stability in model system tests, with decay rates of ca. 2.1 and ca. 0.9 mV h⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.description: Long-term stability HER/OER at 500-1000 mA cm⁻² in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Ni₃S₂/NM-I serving as bifunctional OER and HER electrodes, maintains >3000 h stable water splitting at 500-1000 mA cm⁻² with negligible activity decay in three-electrode configurations (Figure 3f), despite sulfur leaching and surface amorphization to NiOOH during OER... The Ni dissolution during 600 h of the OER test at 500 mA cm⁻² is nearly zero

nodes.description: Mechanical stability ultrasonic test in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Mechanical stability testing under aggressive ultrasonic agitation (400 W, 1.0 M KOH, 25 °C) demonstrates exceptional robustness: Ni₃S₂/NM-I retains 97.4% mass after 400 min

nodes.description: ADT anode testing in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: For anode testing (Figure 4b), Ni₃S₂/NM-I demonstrates exceptional stability over 4000 ADT cycles, with activity enhancement

nodes.description: ADT cathode testing in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Similar trends emerge for cathodes (Figures 4d and S29), where Ni₃S₂/NM-I maintains near-zero activity loss

nodes.description: Zero-gap AWE performance 30 wt% KOH at 80°C
nodes.source_text: At 80 °C in 30 wt% KOH, the Ni₃S₂/NM I∥Ni₃S₂/NM I system achieves low cell voltages of 1.72 and 1.79 V at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻², respectively (Figure 6a), surpassing routine Raney nickel/NM (R-Ni/NM)∥NM... Long-term stability tests under industrial operating conditions (1000 mA cm⁻², 80 °C) reveal zero voltage decay over 1500 h (Figure 6b)... the Ni₃S₂/NM-I∥Ni₃S₂/NM-I system exhibits remarkable fluctuating resistance, maintaining stable operation for over 1200 h (3600 startup/shutdown cycles)

nodes.description: LSV electrochemical measurements in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The electrochemical test was performed on a CS310X electrochemical workstation with a three-electrode configuration. The working, reference, and counter electrodes were the prepared sample, the Hg/HgO electrode, and the platinum plate, respectively. A cyclic voltammetry (CV) scan was carried out at a scan rate of 100 mV s⁻¹, and then a linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) test was performed at a scan rate of 2 mV s⁻¹, accompanied by an iR compensation of 60%.
Double layer capacitance (Cdl) was obtained by measuring CVs at a scan rate of 5 to 150 mV s⁻¹.
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was obtained at 5 mV amplitude with a frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 1 MHz (at -0.15 V vs RHE for HER and 1.38 V vs RHE for OER).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni3S2/NM-I and Ni3S2/NM-H both crystallize in the heazlewoodite Ni3S2 phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both systems crystallize in the heazlewoodite Ni3S2 phase (Figures S12a and S14a).

nodes.characterization_summary: IL-TEM images show time-dependent surface amorphization of Ni@Ni3S2 NPs at 1.3 V vs RHE with oxygen incorporation and sulfur depletion after 10h and 20h OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Identical location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) experiments conducted at 1.3 V (vs RHE) in 1.0 M KOH further reveal time-dependent surface amorphization concurrent with oxygen incorporation and sulfur depletion (Figures 2a,b and S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns confirm structural changes in Ni@Ni3S2 NPs after 10h and 20h OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) of (a4) pristine Ni@Ni3S2 NPs, (a5) after 10 h OER, and (a6) after 20 h OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS quantitative results show changes in Ni, S, and O elemental composition for Ni@Ni3S2 NPs before and after 10 and 20 h OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) quantitative results of Ni, S, and O elements for Ni@Ni3S2 NPs before and after 10 and 20 h OER.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution S 2p XPS spectra for Ni@Ni3S2 NPs show complete signal attenuation after 100 h OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution S 2p XPS spectra for Ni@Ni3S2 NPs before and after 100 h OER.

nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near-edge spectra (XANES) of Ni@Ni3S2 NPs after 100 h of OER exhibit a positively shifted absorption edge, higher than that of the NiO reference (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT of Ni K-edge EXAFS shows main peak change from Ni-S bond at ~1.85 Å to Ni-O bond at ~1.63 Å after OER for Ni@Ni3S2 NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier transform (FT) of Ni K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra (Figure 2e), the main peak of Ni@Ni3S2 NPs after OER changes from the Ni-S bond at ~1.85 Å to the Ni-O bond at ~1.63 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM confirms seamless interfacial binding between Ni3S2 layer and nickel substrate in Ni3S2/NM-I.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The interfacial nanostructure was further characterized by SEM and TEM after focused ion beam (FIB) processing.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional TEM image confirms ~80 nm dense interlayer at catalyst-substrate interface forming composition-gradient architecture in Ni3S2/NM-I.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cross-sectional TEM image confirms the seamless interfacial binding between the Ni3S2 layer and the nickel substrate (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image of interfacial region of Ni3S2/NM-I shows three components: metallic Ni substrate, Ni3S2 top layer, and transitional zone.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3d1 presents the high-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image of the interfacial region of Ni3S2/NM-I.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS mappings identify metallic Ni substrate with Ni0 signals, Ni3S2 top layer with Niδ+ and S2- signals, and transitional zone with metallic Ni NPs in Ni3S2/NM-I.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding EELS mappings clearly identify three components: (i) the metallic Ni substrate with Ni0 EELS signals, (ii) the Ni3S2 top layer enriched with Niδ+ and S2- signals, and (iii) a transitional zone populated by metallic Ni NPs infilling Ni3S2 vacancies (Figure 3d2-d4).

nodes.characterization_summary: DPC-STEM phase mapping from 4D-STEM data confirms crystallographic interfaces: blue=Ni substrate, green=Ni3S2 catalytic layer, transition color=composition-gradient interlayer in Ni3S2/NM-I.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The differential phase contrast (DPC) image obtained by 4D-STEM further confirms the formation of crystallographic interfaces across these regions (Figure 3d5).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman spectra capture dynamic formation of NiIII-O vibrational peaks at 1.3 V vs RHE diagnostic of catalytically active NiOOH species for Ni@Ni3S2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectra tests directly capture the dynamic formation of NiIII-O vibrational peaks at a potential of 1.3 V vs reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) (Figure S6), diagnostic of catalytically active NiOOH species.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman spectroscopy of post-ADT Ni3S2/NM-I anodes shows stable NiOOH peaks at 480 and 559 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectroscopy of post-ADT Ni3S2/NM-I anodes shows stable peaks at 480 and 559 cm⁻¹ (Figure 4g), characteristic of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional HRTEM images and SAED pattern show Ni/Ni3S2 interlayer structure remains intact after 4000 ADT cycles for Ni3S2/NM-I cathode.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cross-sectional HRTEM images and SAED pattern of Ni3S2/NM-I after 4000 ADT cycles as (e) the cathode and (f) the anode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping of Ni3S2/NM-I shows uniform distribution of S element on nickel wire surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental mapping of Ni3S2/NM-I exhibits uniform distribution of the S element on the surface of an individual nickel wire (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-test XRD confirms structural integrity of Ni3S2/NM-I after mechanical stability testing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Post-test XRD and SEM characterizations confirm the structural integrity of Ni3S2/NM-I (Figure S15).
